ScreenshotsHint: Select a thumbnail to preview. Removed screenshots leave your original files untouched.
ImagesUploadHint: Choose how to add images, then browse or drop JPG, PNG or BMP files here. When adding a cover, remaining images become screenshots.
ImagesCoverHint: Add up to 10 images, including the cover. Click + or drag images here. Hover a thumbnail to delete it or use the picture-frame button to set it as the cover. The cover moves to the first position.
ImagesLimit: Each game can have up to 10 images, including its cover. Remove an image before adding more.
ImageDeleteScreenshot: Remove this screenshot from the game? Original image files will be kept.
ImageDeleteCover: Remove this cover from the game? The next image will become the cover. Original image files will be kept.
GameGenreHint: Choose the genre used in the game list and genre filters. Changes save automatically.
GenreManagerHint: Select a genre to rename it, or enter a new name and choose Add genre. Names are shared by all games and genre filters.
GenreDuplicate: A genre with this name already exists.
GenreDeleteMessage: Remove {0}? {1} game(s) will be moved to Uncategorized.
GenreDeleteHint: Deleting a genre moves its games to Uncategorized. Game files are kept.
GenreMenuHint: Select a genre, then use Edit or Delete. Use Add genre to create a new one.
GenreChineseDuplicate: A genre with this Chinese name already exists.
GenreChineseHint: Shown when Chinese is selected. Leave blank to use the English name.
GameDeveloperHint: Company or team that developed the game.
ImageFileShared: This image is also used by another game. Remove it from that game before deleting the file.
ImageFileDeleteFailed: Image removed, but its file could not be deleted: {0}
ImageCoverRemovalChoice: Remove this cover? The next image will become the cover. Choose whether to keep or permanently delete the image file.
ImageScreenshotRemovalChoice: Remove this screenshot? Choose whether to keep or permanently delete the image file.
LaunchIntro: Original DOSBox configuration values and imported game options are loaded into the controls. Open a section to inspect them; enable customization to save changes for this game.
LaunchStartupHint: Select the game’s EXE, COM, or BAT file. For games with a launcher, select its BAT file.
LaunchVersionHint: Automatic uses the imported version or your global default. Register additional versions in Settings.
LaunchOverrideHint: On: use the profile below instead of the imported launch options. Off: restore the original imported options. Your game files are never edited.
LaunchInheritance: “Use DOSBox configuration” leaves that setting to the selected DOSBox and its configuration files. It does not copy the imported game option.
LaunchResetHint: Start a clean profile: clear extra options, disc mounts, and custom paths; keep the registered version.
LaunchCyclesHint: Blank: use DOSBox config. Start with auto. If an old game runs too fast, try 3000 and adjust. max uses as much CPU as possible and can make timing-sensitive games too fast.
LaunchCoreHint: Normal favors compatibility. Dynamic can improve demanding games but may break some software; switch back if it crashes.
LaunchMemoryHint: 16 MB suits many DOS games. Increase only if the game needs more; some older games reject large memory sizes.
LaunchEmsHint: Enable if the game asks for EMS. Disable only for a documented compatibility requirement.
LaunchXmsHint: Many later DOS games need XMS. Keep the emulator’s setting unless the game’s manual says otherwise.
LaunchUmbHint: Provides upper-memory blocks used by some DOS software. Usually leave this inherited.
LaunchScreenHint: Choose explicitly between windowed and fullscreen, or follow the global launcher preference. Alt+Enter switches while playing.
LaunchMachineHint: SVGA (S3) is a common starting point. Use VGA, EGA, CGA, or Tandy only when the game needs that hardware.
LaunchOutputHint: Try OpenGL for scaling. Surface is a basic fallback and does not support aspect correction in classic DOSBox. Available outputs vary by DOSBox build.
LaunchAspectHint: Use with a scaling output to restore the intended proportions of many 320×200 games.
LaunchFramesHint: 0 draws every frame. Higher values reduce rendering work but make movement less smooth; use only if performance is poor.
LaunchAudioIntro: The game’s own SETUP or INSTALL program must select the same sound card, port, IRQ, and DMA. These controls do not change the game’s setup files.
LaunchSoundHint: Choose the card supported by the game. Sound Blaster 16 is common; older games may need Sound Blaster Pro or earlier.
LaunchOplHint: Auto follows the sound card. Use OPL2 for AdLib-era music, or OPL3 when the game supports it.
LaunchMidiHint: Select the MPU-401 interface expected by the game. A working MIDI output device or synthesizer must also be configured in DOSBox.
LaunchSoundValues: Match the game’s setup. A common combination is port 220, IRQ 7, DMA 1, high DMA 5.
LaunchJoystickHint: Auto detects a controller. Choose None if the game has drifting controls or incorrectly detects a joystick.
LaunchSensitivityHint: Blank: use DOSBox config. 100 is normal speed; lower values slow the mouse. Accepted range: 1–1000.
LaunchMediaHint: The game folder is always drive C. Add drive D only if the game requires a CD. The floppy option launches the game folder as drive A or B.
LaunchMediaPathHint: Choose a file or folder inside the game folder, or type its relative path (for example cd/disc.cue). For CUE/BIN discs, select the CUE file and keep its referenced BIN files beside it. For CD folders, “no” uses the game folder itself.
LaunchFloppyHint: Mounts the game folder as a floppy, not a floppy image. Bootable disk images need an advanced configuration.
LaunchMediaOutside: Choose media inside this game’s folder, or use an advanced configuration for other locations.
LaunchExeHint: Usually leave blank to use the registered version above. Set this only for a separate DOSBox EXE needed by this game.
LaunchConfigHint: Optional .conf or .cfg file for build-specific options, custom mounts, or MIDI output. It loads after the registered config; selections above take priority. Existing files are never rewritten.
LaunchRawHint: Advanced: comma-separated name,value pairs such as core,normal,ems,false. The controls above edit these same options. Unknown options are rejected; put build-specific settings in a configuration file.
LaunchExit: Close DOSBox when the game finishes
LaunchExitHint: Off keeps the DOS prompt available for troubleshooting. This runs EXIT after the startup program returns.
LaunchSkipHint: Ignores [autoexec] commands in configuration files. Use this if an existing config starts another game or mounts conflicting drives. The launcher’s own game commands still run.
LaunchGuide: Help · Which settings should I change?
LaunchGuideText: Start with your existing settings. If the game runs too fast, lower CPU cycles; if it crashes with Dynamic, use Normal. For missing sound, run the game’s SETUP and match its card and IRQ/DMA here. For a missing CD message, select the correct disc image or folder. Change one setting at a time and launch the game to check it. Ctrl+F11 / Ctrl+F12 adjust speed in classic DOSBox; Ctrl+F9 quits it. Hotkeys and supported options can differ in other builds.
LaunchCheckHint: Checks saved paths and option values; it does not run the game or guarantee compatibility.
LaunchChoice23: Select a CD image inside the game folder
LaunchPortHint: Hexadecimal I/O address. 220 is common; match the address selected in the game’s setup.
LaunchIrqHint: Interrupt line. 7 or 5 are common; the game and DOSBox must use the same value.
LaunchDmaHint: 8-bit DMA channel, commonly 1. Match the game’s digital sound configuration.
LaunchHdmaHint: 16-bit DMA channel for Sound Blaster 16, commonly 5. Older sound cards do not use this setting.
LaunchFullResolutionHint: Desktop uses the monitor’s current resolution. Or enter width x height without spaces, for example 1920x1080. Blank uses the DOSBox config.
LaunchWindowResolutionHint: Set the scaled window size, for example 1280x960. Original uses the game’s native size. Blank uses the DOSBox config.
LaunchResolutionInfo: Resolution settings scale the display; they do not increase the game’s native graphics resolution. Choose a scaling video output such as OpenGL below. Surface does not support these size overrides in classic DOSBox.
LaunchImportedMissingValue: Ignored incomplete imported option: {0}. No value was assumed.
LaunchImportedExtraCycles: Ignored extra imported CPU cycles value: {0}. Kept the first value.
LaunchOriginalMissing: No original configuration file found. Imported options are shown; other values are left to DOSBox.
LaunchOriginalUnreadable: Original DOSBox configuration could not be read. Imported game options are still shown.
